newsitem.title: SPAIN: ETA kidnap victim near death, Spaniards outraged.
newsitem.headline: ETA kidnap victim near death, Spaniards outraged.

text.p: A young politician kidnapped and shot in the head by Basque separatists was close to death on Sunday, and thousands of Spaniards expressed their outrage in overnight protests and candle-light vigils.

Miguel Angel Blanco, a 29-year-old Basque town councillor and low-ranking member of Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar's ruling Popular Party, was not expected to survive for long, a San Sebastian hospital spokesman said.
Blanco was in a deep coma and showing signs of "brain death", said the spokesman.
Doctors believed his case was so hopeless they decided against operating to remove the two bullets lodged in his brain.
"The prognosis is very grave," said Dr Inaki Azcuna, head of the health department for the Basque regional government.
Family members anxiously awaited word on Blanco's fate. They had been told earlier by officials, mistakenly, that he was dead.

The Basque guerrilla group ETA kidnapped Blanco on Thursday and said they would kill him at 4 p.m. (1400 GMT) on Saturday unless the government transferred some 500 ETA inmates to prisons in the Basque country.
Government officials said they would never give in to blackmail.
Soon after the deadline passed, a hunter heard gunshots in a wooded area outside San Sebastian and found Blanco dumped on a country lane, bound and bloodied.
Blanco's ordeal touched a raw nerve among Spaniards, who in recent months have faced a growing wave of violence by ETA which has killed 800 people in a nearly 30-year fight for independence.
In a series of marches and rallies, hundreds of thousands of Spaniards turned out across the country on Saturday in a show of solidarity with Blanco and in opposition to ETA.
In the Basque capital Bilbao alone, half a million people led by Aznar demonstrated against ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom).
Protests continued into the early hours on Sunday, with large crowds taking to the streets in over a dozen cities. In central Madrid, more than 50,000 people chanted "Murderers! Murderers!".
The front pages of Spain's Sunday newspapers were brimming with anger. "Sons of Bitches," declared a headline in Diario 16. "Beasts!" said another in the YA newspaper.
Leading politicians denounced ETA's action and urged calm. "The government expresses its strongest condemnation against this barbarity," said government spokesman Miguel Angel.
On Saturday night, unidentified attackers firebombed an office belonging to ETA's political wing, Herri Batasuna, in Blanco's hometown of Ermua, but little damage was caused.

Organisers of Pamplona's world-famous running of the bulls suspended the festival on Saturday in support of Blanco. It was the first such interruption since 1978 when it was cancelled after clashes between police and Basque nationalist demonstrators.
A Vatican spokesman told Spanish state radio that Pope John Paul was praying for Blanco and his family.
Basque political parties planned to meet on Sunday to discuss a response to ETA's action. The government has called a meeting of a multi-party anti-terrorist group on Monday.
Authorities said Blanco was probably targeted because he was a member of the ruling centre-right Popular Party but, as a low-level official, was not protected by bodyguards.

In Blanco's hometown, people wept in the streets on Saturday afternoon when officials announced he had been found dead. But less than an hour later, word came through that he had survived the attack but was in an extremely critical condition.

After the shooting, Basque nationalist leader Jose Antonio Ardanza angrily criticised ETA's political wing. "It's time for (ETA) to be denounced publicly. Herri Batasuna, you always want to be presented as victims in this society but you are the executioners," Ardanza told a news conference.

ETA is seeking an independent Basque state encompassing parts of northern Spain and southern France. The rebels have set deadlines to execute kidnap victims twice before, in 1981 and 1983, and in both cases the hostages were killed.
